clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A hospital uses Universal Precautions for handling all blood and OPIM specimens. A closed, leak-resistant specimen tube is recognizable as a specimen and will remain within the hospital. Which statement about OSHA biohazard labeling is accurate?

options.A: OSHA permits the specimen-labeling/color-coding exemption while the recognizable container remains within the facility.
options.B: OSHA requires a biohazard label on every individual specimen tube even when the within-facility exemption applies.
options.C: OSHA permits the same exemption when the recognizable specimen is shipped from the hospital to an outside facility.
options.D: OSHA bases the labeling requirement on whether the client's infection status is known to be positive.

semantic_correction.rationale: OSHA requires blood and OPIM specimens to be placed in containers that prevent leakage. For storage, transport, or shipping, containers are generally labeled or color-coded and closed. However, when a facility uses Universal Precautions for all specimens, OSHA permits labeling/color-coding to be omitted for containers that are recognizable as containing specimens while they remain within that facility. OSHA explicitly states that this exemption does not apply when specimens leave the facility. The rule is based on specimen handling and containment, not the individual client's known infection status. This biohazard-labeling rule is separate from patient-identification labeling requirements.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Apply OSHA's limited within-facility Universal Precautions exemption for recognizable blood/OPIM specimen containers and recognize that the exemption ends when specimens leave the facility.
semantic_correction.source_version_date: Current federal OSHA standard accessed August 21, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(xiii) and (d)(2)(xiii)(A) — leak-preventing specimen container, labeling/color-coding, within-facility Universal Precautions exemption, off-site labeling requirement; §1910.1030(g)(1)(i)(G) — individual-container labeling exemption when enclosed in an appropriately labeled larger container
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: Recognizable specimen containers may be exempt from biohazard labeling/color-coding while remaining within a facility that uses Universal Precautions for all specimens; the exemption does not extend to specimens leaving the facility.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: converted the long multi-rule recall item into a specific within-facility specimen scenario, removed absolute distractor wording, and explicitly separated OSHA biohazard labeling from patient-identification labeling to prevent construct ambiguity.

audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p. 24
audit_findings_append.finding: The original answer bundled two OSHA exemptions and was uniquely longest. The revised item tests the within-facility Universal Precautions exemption in a bounded scenario and avoids implying that patient-identification labels may be omitted.

option_audit.A: Correct. OSHA expressly permits this biohazard-labeling/color-coding exemption for recognizable specimens remaining within a Universal Precautions facility.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. The regulation explicitly provides a within-facility exemption under the stated conditions.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. OSHA states that labeling or color-coding is required when such specimens leave the facility.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Universal Precautions treat relevant blood/body-fluid exposure as potentially infectious regardless of known client infection status.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. The stem fixes all prerequisites for the OSHA within-facility exemption and specifies that the specimen remains within the hospital.
cueing_check: All four options address the scope of the OSHA labeling exemption and are comparable in length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
